text:
laura (support): P1 from Acme — rerank endpoint spiking with 5xx/timeouts during peak customer traffic. Customer saw p95 go from ~120ms to ~1.8s and ~3-5% 502/504s. They reported increased retries from their side which made it worse.

laura (support): Key details: QPS ~800 steady, bursts to 1500 qps for 30-60s. Candidate lists sometimes >200 items. Payloads ~80-150KB. Happens mostly between 16:00-16:30 UTC.

laura (support): Example curl they sent:
```
POST /v1/rerank
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model":"rerank-v2",
  "query":"...",
  "candidates":["..." x 180]
}
```

jorge (sre): thanks — can you paste the X-Request-ID or request timestamps for one failure? also which region/cluster?

laura (support): sent one request-id in DM: rq_20260317_9a7c. Region: us-west-2, cluster: rerank-prod-v2.

infra-bot: ALERT: rerank-gateway error-rate >3% (5xx) for service rerank-prod-v2. p95 latency 1.82s (+1.6s). rolling window 5m.

maya (eng-runtime): quick guesses: 1) very large candidate lists increase backend work and KV cache miss rates 2) gateway retry/backoff loop causing fan-out 3) per-pod concurrency saturation. Do we see GC/alloc spikes on pods?

jorge (sre): checking logs for rq_20260317_9a7c... found repeated upstream timeouts then gateway retry attempts:
```
[16:12:04] upstream_timeout id=rq_20260317_9a7c backend=rerank-worker-12
[16:12:04] gateway_retry id=rq_20260317_9a7c attempt=1
[16:12:05] upstream_timeout id=rq_20260317_9a7c backend=rerank-worker-7
[16:12:05] gateway_retry id=rq_20260317_9a7c attempt=2
[16:12:06] circuit_breaker_open cluster=rerank-prod-v2
```

maya (eng-runtime): that pattern matches a retry storm: gateway retries while backend is overloaded -> more load -> more timeouts. Also if candidates >128 we don't use prefix KV cache effectively, leading to repeated full rerank compute.

sophie (prod): customer is hitting contract limits? they said no auth errors. Billing looks fine. but they were doing parallel fanout from their side (30 concurrent client threads).

laura (support): customer confirms parallelism from their side. they can throttle but want a mitigation on our side first.

maya (eng-runtime): short-term mitigations to propose:
- enforce request-level candidate cap (suggest 100) at gateway with 413 + helpful error
- disable automatic gateway retries for rerank route (or set conservative retry=0-1 + exponential backoff with jitter)
- route large requests to dedicated capacity pool (if customer on Dedicated)
- add quick KV-prefetch for candidate lists >32 (if possible)

jorge (sre): operational mitigations I'll apply now: set per-route retry_count=0 for /v1/rerank in us-west-2 and add rate-limit to 1200 qps burst 300 -> will roll for 5m. creating runbook entry.

laura (support): noted, telling customer we'll apply gateway tweaks and ask them to temporarily reduce client concurrency to 8.

infra-bot: CONFIG_CHANGE: route /v1/rerank retries=0 applied to us-west-2 by jorge at 16:34 UTC.

maya (eng-runtime): longer-term: consider server-side batching / adaptive batching and smarter per-request cost estimate. Also add a circuit-breaker metric that proxies backpressure to clients (429) before 5xx. We should also measure candidate-size distribution to set a safe default cap.

laura (support): customer accepted temporary throttle; still seeing a few 502s but error rate dropped to ~0.6%. they will schedule to reduce concurrency tomorrow.

jorge (sre): follow-up items created: INC-2026-123 (rerank p95 retry-oscillation), assign eng-runtime, priority P1 for fix PRs. repro plan: run load test with 1500 qps and candidate sizes [32,64,128,200] with gateway retries enabled vs disabled.

maya (eng-runtime): logging repro harness notes: use rerank-harness v3, env var RERANK_CANDIDATE_LIMIT to simulate. will capture perf counters: kv_cache_hit, per-request tokens, pod_cpu, avg_latency. scheduling run at 18:00 UTC.

laura (support): will send customer update after the 18:00 repro and share any config changes. thanks all. :thumbsup:

jorge (sre): postmortem hypothesis: root cause = combination of large candidate lists (>128) + client-side parallelism + gateway retries -> retry amplification. Next steps: enforce candidate cap, disable retries, improve caching heuristics, document best-practice on support KB.

sophie (prod): +1 on KB. also add a quick note to onboarding docs warning about candidate fan-out and recommended client-side concurrency defaults (<=8).

laura (support): ACTIONS: 1) tell customer temp throttle applied 2) ask them to reduce client concurrency to <=8 3) share postmortem and KB link when ready.

maya (eng-runtime): putting a small PR to set default candidate max 128 and runtime flag to enable aggressive prefix caching. will link PR in the incident.

laura (support): closing loop with customer now. will reopen thread if anything regresses.

sophie (prod): FYI forwarded to account team and AE.

laura (support): resolved for now, keeping incident open for follow-up fixes. :white_check_mark:
